en.title: Tignes powder forecast next week (23–29 November 2026): 29 cm up top
en.description: Next week's fresh snow in Tignes: 11–48 cm on the upper slopes and 8–38 cm at the base (23–29 November 2026), best day, best slopes and how sure the forecast is.
en.lede: Thursday 26 November is the day to circle for Tignes. It carries the biggest single share of next week's snow, and over the whole week of 23–29 November the top around 3300 m collects 29 cm (11–48 cm) while the base gets 23 cm.

sections.h: This week in Tignes: the set-up
p: Next week does not start from scratch. From Tuesday 17 to Friday 20 November our forecast gives the top 98 cm (78–118 cm) and the base 38 cm, the bigger fall of the fortnight. By the time the next round arrives, the upper mountain should already carry a real cover.
Read from the top down: 29 cm near 3300 m, 26 cm near 2500 m, 23 cm near 1700 m. The low-to-high spread is 11–48 cm at the top and 8–38 cm at the base.

Most of the total arrives on Wednesday 25 (6 cm, up to 7), Thursday 26 (9 cm, up to 15), Saturday 28 (3 cm, up to 5) and Sunday 29 (6 cm, up to 12), counted at the top as the middle of our forecast and the high case.
The base gets nearly as much as the top (23 against 29 cm), which means the snow line stays below the lowest lifts for most of the week. Snow down to the village is the likely picture.
Tignes le Lac sits high on its plateau, so the resort itself rarely sees rain once the season turns.
For comparison, the upper slopes of the closest big resorts collect Val d'Isère (6 km away) 28 cm, Les Arcs (14 km away) 29 cm and La Plagne (17 km away) 28 cm; Tignes sits at 29 cm.
Snow will not decide between these resorts next week. Height, aspect and which lifts are open will.

Thursday 26 November is the snowiest day up top: 9 cm in the middle of our forecast and up to 15 cm in the high case. The morning after a snowy day is usually the one to ski, once lifts and patrols have caught up.

Go high: depth is safest on the Grande Motte glacier above Val Claret, and the best skiing should be on the high runs off the Grande Motte and the cold slopes around the lake. Treat the lower runs to Tignes les Brévières, the lowest corner of the area as the weak point.
Reasonably, with a caveat. The snow is coming to Tignes, but the top could end up anywhere between 11 and 48 cm, and the middle value of 29 cm is only the halfway mark.
Book flexibly if you can: the picture for Tignes will be much sharper by the weekend.

advice: Fresh snow on a young snowpack: read the French avalanche bulletin (BERA) for the massif before any off-piste plan.
Check the resort's own opening date and lift status: snow on the mountain does not mean lifts are running.
Plan around the top's 29 cm, and keep the high case of 48 cm as a bonus.
